discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid-Mott insulator transition to single-site quantum gas microscopy

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitat Munchen and Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and co-workers) showed theoretically in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Greiner, Bloch and colleagues observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator, the first time a strongly correlated lattice model was realized cleanly and controllably. This founded the field of analog quantum simulation. The nominees went on to lead it: Bloch through studies of Fermi-Hubbard physics, many-body localization and artificial gauge fields; Greiner by inventing the quantum gas microscope, which images individual atoms on single lattice sites and revealed antiferromagnetic order and entanglement directly; Zoller through foundational proposals that link quantum simulation and quantum computing. Their work turned Feynman's vision into a working laboratory tool. It answers questions that are intractable in solids, and it underpins today's neutral-atom quantum processors.
